content.text:
I fixed the missing seam, but I couldn't check it visually in the editor yet because your dev server on 5187 needs a restart (explained below).

**Why the seam was missing:** The seam is drawn in each button's own border color. Primary buttons have a border the same color as their fill (both `rgb(29, 53, 79)` in the rebrand theme), so the seam is there but you can't see it. Bare, danger, and success buttons have the same problem.

**Fix:** I added a rule at the end of [button-set.css](plugins/pantoken/custom-components/src/components/button-set/button-set.css). For those solid-fill buttons, the seam now uses the label color at 35% opacity, so it shows as a lighter line against the fill. The rule skips:
- `-without-seam` sets
- disabled and pressed buttons
- `-on-color`, `-condensed`, `-without-background`, and `-without-border` buttons
- secondary, tertiary, and the AI variants, which still use their own border as the seam

I also updated the component's doc comment and the existing [button-set-seam.md](.changeset/button-set-seam.md) changeset.

**Checks:** I rebuilt the plugin with `vp run build` and its 35 tests pass. On a test page, the new rule applied to exactly the buttons it should. That page didn't load the theme styles, though, so I haven't seen how it looks.

**Your dev server needs a restart:** Partway through, I ran a bare `vp pack`, which clears `dist` and briefly removed `model.json`. Your server on 5187 tried to load it during that gap and now fails with "Failed to resolve import `@pantoken/plugin-custom-components/model.json`". The file is back, but the server keeps showing the error until it restarts. I didn't restart it because it's your process. After restarting, check the seam in both rebrand and canvas.

content.text:
It's not the tooltip. [tooltip.css](formats/components/src/components/tooltip/tooltip.css#L24-L27) only sets `position: relative` and `display: inline-flex` on the button, plus styles for the `.tip` child. It doesn't touch borders, background, or color.

The button-set rules were already applying in the app before my change. When I checked the styles the browser actually applied to the three buttons:
- **Corners:** only the outer two were rounded (`12px 0 0 12px` on the first, `0 12px 12px 0` on the last).
- **Joins:** the doubled border was collapsed (`border-inline-start-width: 0px` on the second and third).
- **Seam:** each button's end border was 1px, but `rgb(29, 53, 79)` for both the border and the fill.

So the seam was drawn, just in the same color as the fill. That's a primary-fill problem, and the label-color tint I added fixes it no matter which other classes the buttons carry.
